system_description.narrative_title: Democratic Midterm Sweep and Its Political‑Economic Ripple Effects
system_description.narrative_summary: A broad Democratic 'blue wave' in the 2026 midterms — flipping House, multiple Senate seats and state offices — is simultaneously reshaping US policy prospects and rattling global markets. The election outcome set off immediate market moves (stock, bond, commodity shifts), empowered investigations and legislative initiatives targeting Trump-era policies and allies, and altered the early dynamics of the 2028 presidential race. This is an open system: political actions, investor reactions, legal challenges and international market feedback will interact and co-evolve over the coming months.
system_description.scope: Federal and state 2026 midterm election results and their direct downstream effects: changes in Congressional and gubernatorial control; immediate market reactions (equities, bonds, commodities); prospective fiscal, tax and regulatory initiatives; congressional investigations and legal/court interactions; and the evolving positioning for the 2028 presidential contest.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic system (international capital markets, geopolitics, and transnational regulatory and investment flows).
adjacent_subsystems: US party and electoral system (parties, primaries, voter coalitions)
Global financial markets and investor sentiment (equities, bonds, commodities, risk premia)
Tech/AI investment and corporate governance ecosystem
US legal and oversight institutions (courts, DOJ, congressional committees)
evidence_headlines: Democrats projected to win majority control of US House, US media project

variables.name: Legislative control balance
variables.description: The relative margin of control within the legislature between the dominant coalition and opposition, measured continuously from minority to supermajority.

variables.name: Executive‑legislative alignment
variables.description: The degree of policy and agenda alignment between the executive branch and the legislature, ranging from strong conflict to strong cooperation.

variables.name: Regulatory direction
variables.description: The net trend in regulatory policy orientation, measured on a spectrum from deregulatory to more restrictive/regulatory tightening.

variables.name: Fiscal policy stance
variables.description: The overall budgetary posture of public finance authorities, from expansionary (higher deficits/spending) to contractionary (austerity/surplus orientation).

variables.name: Tax policy uncertainty
variables.description: Perceived uncertainty about current and prospective tax rules, rates and enforcement, measured as expected variance and unpredictability.

variables.name: Investor risk sentiment
variables.description: Aggregate market participants' appetite for risk versus safety, measured continuously from risk‑averse to risk‑seeking.

variables.name: Asset price volatility
variables.description: The realized or implied short‑to‑medium term volatility across major asset classes, indicating market stability or turbulence.

variables.name: Long‑term bond yields
variables.description: Prevailing long‑duration fixed‑income yield levels that reflect time value of money and macroeconomic expectations.

variables.name: Currency strength
variables.description: The relative value and purchasing‑power strength of the domestic currency versus a broad set of external currencies and baskets.

variables.name: Cross‑border capital flows
variables.description: Net flows of private and public capital crossing borders (investment, portfolio and banking flows) measured per unit time.

variables.name: Investigative activity intensity
variables.description: The rate and intensity of formal oversight, inquiries and investigatory actions directed at policy actors and past decisions.

variables.name: Legal proceedings risk
variables.description: The perceived probability and expected impact of legal actions, injunctions and litigation that affect policy actors or policy outcomes.

variables.name: Electoral mobilization momentum
variables.description: The momentum of voter engagement and campaign mobilization efforts, measured as a changing rate of turnout and organizational activation.

variables.name: Media framing intensity
variables.description: The degree to which media coverage amplifies, polarizes or reframes political and economic issues, measured by reach and framing extremity.

variables.name: Policy commitment clarity
variables.description: The clarity and credibility of policy signals and commitments from policymakers, ranging from ambiguous/contradictory to clear/credible.

variables.name: Trade policy orientation
variables.description: The prevailing orientation of trade policy from liberalizing/open to protectionist/restrictive, measured as a continuous policy stance.

catalysts.title: New Congress convenes (Jan 3, 2027)
catalysts.description: Swearing-in of the new Democratic-controlled Congress, enabling committee jurisdiction, legislative agenda-setting and oversight powers.
catalysts.rationale: Democrats projected to win House and Senate majorities; headlines on Democratic sweep and plans to reshape Congress.

catalysts.title: Senate hearing for Fed nominee Lisa Cook (Dec 14, 2026)
catalysts.description: Delayed White House panel hearing on Fed nominee Lisa Cook could influence market expectations about Fed policy and clarity around the FOMC's tilt.
catalysts.rationale: White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14 (headline).

catalysts.title: 2027 federal tax bracket and capital-gains changes take effect
catalysts.description: IRS-set 2027 tax brackets, capital-gains and estate/gift changes come into force at the new tax year, altering tax liabilities and planning.
catalysts.rationale: IRS unveils higher capital gains brackets and new federal income brackets for 2027 (headlines).

catalysts.title: Democratic congressional probes into Trump deals and JPMorgan
catalysts.description: Committees plan investigations of Trump-related deals and bank relationships (JPMorgan/Epstein) after Democrats take control, triggering oversight and possible legal referrals.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democrats to investigate Trump deals' and 'Democrats to probe JPMorgan's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein'.

catalysts.title: Mississippi Senate razor‑thin race legal fight
catalysts.description: Ongoing recounts and legal challenges in Mississippi could change a Senate seat outcome and alter the chamber margin.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Mississippi Senate: Colom, Hyde-Smith gird for ballot legal fight in razor-thin race'.

catalysts.title: Risk of 2027 debt‑ceiling standoff
catalysts.description: Market attention to a potential debt‑limit showdown under a newly shifted congressional balance could raise volatility and push yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Investors eye risk of debt-ceiling standoff after Democratic sweep'.

catalysts.title: Plan to roll back Trump-era Canada tariffs
catalysts.description: Democratic leaders are reportedly drafting steps to reverse tariffs on Canada, shifting the trade agenda and cross-border flows if enacted.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Exclusive | Democrats Are Hatching a Plan to Reverse Trump’s Canada Tariffs'.

catalysts.title: Heightened regulatory scrutiny of crypto, AI and data centres
catalysts.description: Post-sweep momentum for oversight threatens tougher regulation and permitting scrutiny for crypto, AI/data centres and related infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democratic sweep puts crypto on defensive', 'Markets fret blue wave will drown data centres', 'Permitting reform is an early test for the Democrats'.

catalysts.title: California billionaire tax measure final count
catalysts.description: State vote tally will decide a high-profile wealth tax measure and influence momentum for wealth taxation debates nationally.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Billionaire tax measure trails as California tallies votes' and 'California’s billionaire tax faces defeat, but Democrats plan higher taxes on the wealthy'.
